DW-264.intent: Make the stack-expiry model AUTHORABLE rather than picking one (Alec, 2026-08-02). Three of the four requested modes ALREADY EXIST in the closed StackRule enum (godot/src/Effects/Modifier.cs:7-15) and need no new work: 'additive timer (re-apply resets the timer)' = StackRule.Refresh; 'single stack only when not stackable' = StackRule.Ignore; 'grouped timer (all stacks expire together)' = today's StackRule.Stack, which scales deltas by _stackCount but shares one _remainingTicks (ModifierStore.cs:151,168-177). The ONLY missing mode is INDIVIDUAL per-stack expiry. Implement by splitting the existing Stack member into two explicit members - a grouped/shared-duration variant preserving exactly today's behavior, and a new independent variant carrying per-stack _remainingTicks - so no shipped content changes meaning. Breaks the single-slot shared-duration SoA; folded into SimChecksum, so this re-baselines goldens: ISOLATE that re-record per the checksum-fold timing rule, do not batch it with the DW-265 energy fold or the Epic-15 15-2/15-3/15-4 moves. Surface the mode in the ability editor's stacking dropdown alongside the existing values, and keep StackRule a closed enum (see the enum-indexed-array touch-site rule: patch BOTH switches AND any (int)enum-indexed arrays). ROUTING (2026-08-03): this is Story 15.12's existing charter ('the stacking design pass: per-stack expiry timers ... with validator/authoring surfaces'), not a standalone sweep bundle - a build decision creates no bundle, it is executed when its story runs.
DW-264.label: Creator-selectable stacking-duration mode (individual / grouped / additive / single)

DW-265.intent: Alec 2026-08-02/03: 'Definitely build it' - energy must regenerate, and an Intelligence-style attribute should drive it so a mana economy can be designed around it (WC3 model: Int scales max mana AND regen; Clarity Potions / Brilliance Aura / mana-burn counterplay all sit on top of that). Today EntityWorld.Energy is written ONLY by the cast debit and the start-full apply (EntityWorld.cs:243,1002, both commented 'no regen'), so every caster is one-tank-per-life. SPLIT DECIDED (Alec 2026-08-03) - this entry now covers ONLY the regen half, which is Story 15.12's existing charter: a flat authored per-unit regen_rate on UnitDefinition + a folded per-tick regen path. That alone fixes one-tank-per-life and covers NON-HERO casters, which in WC3 also used flat regen rather than attributes. Energy is folded into SimChecksum so this re-baselines goldens: isolate that re-record per the checksum-fold timing rule, and keep it separate from the DW-264 stacking fold in the same story. Build 15.12's regen path so the rate is read through a single seam that a later attribute system can drive instead of the flat authored value - do NOT hardcode the flat field at the tick site. The attribute system itself is NOT this entry and NOT Story 15.12: hero primary attributes do not exist in the codebase (HeroDefinition carries only flat *_per_level; no Strength/Agility/Intelligence anywhere in godot/src), and Alec's requirement is that CREATORS author their own attribute model, seeded with modern ARPG presets. Filed as Story 15.21 (creator-authorable hero attribute system, full implementation).
DW-265.label: Build energy regeneration (Story 15.12); hero attributes split to their own story

DW-405.intent: Alec 2026-08-02, emphatic: 'Multiplayer online building required - we must be able to perform everything online that we could offline. We're building the game to be multiplayer.' So take the PROPER fix, NOT the option-1 stopgap: MainScene.cs:1010 currently calls _buildSys.QueueWorkerBuild(...) directly - spending resources and setting CommandState=Build, both folded into SimChecksum - bypassing the _lockstep.EnqueueOrder seam every other order uses, so any online build placement desyncs immediately (N-player online at MpSeatCeiling=4 is live and unguarded TODAY). Add a build-order variant to the lockstep order vocabulary carrying BuildingType + placement position (EnqueueOrder's UnitCommand has no such variant; 9.5 excluded it) and route worker-build through it, matching WC3's model where EVERY command goes through one order queue and there is no local fast-path. Do NOT ship option 1 as the end state - blocking online building would make an online match a fixed-army skirmish rather than an RTS. Triage names Story 9.7/9.15 as the home for this plumbing. NOTE: the desync is live until this lands - if it will not be the next bundle dispatched, consider landing the option-1 guard as a temporary safety net in the meantime.
DW-405.label: Add a build-order variant and route worker-build through EnqueueOrder
